title: The Disturbing Disappearance of Tara Calico
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 1989 disappearance of 19-year-old Tara Calico, a University of New Mexico student who vanished on a bike ride near Belen, New Mexico, in September. They walk through the known facts (last seen on Highway 47, reported being followed by an old pickup, bike tracks suggesting it was dragged, a Boston cassette and possible walkman piece found), her mother Patty Dole's lifelong search, and the stepfather and sister's continued efforts. They discuss the 1990 Polaroid of two bound kids found in Port St. Joe, Florida, which some linked to Calico and Michael Henley, and why it remains disputed. They then cover later developments: Sheriff Renee Rivera's 2008 press conference, blogger Melinda Escobell's claims and threats, the 2010 state police inquiry, the 2013 statement from Frank Methola about Henry Brown's deathbed claim implicating Lawrence Romero Jr., and a 2019 FBI reward. The episode closes with a listener mail correction about phone number math and a sign-off.

segments.title: Book plug and case introduction
segments.summary: Hosts plug their book, then introduce the Tara Calico disappearance as a true crime episode with trigger warnings.

segments.title: Tara Calico's disappearance and initial search
segments.summary: Tara Calico, 19, vanished on a bike ride from Belen, New Mexico, last seen on Highway 47 around 11:45, reportedly followed by an old truck. Bike tracks suggested the bike was dragged. Her mother Patty Dole's worry and the family's later deputization are described.

segments.title: Scant evidence and search efforts
segments.summary: Reported findings include a Boston cassette tape and a possible walkman piece, neither firmly tied to Calico. Her rings, shoes and bike were never found. Searches of the area were conducted.

segments.title: The Port St. Joe Polaroid
segments.summary: A Polaroid of two bound, taped children in a white van was found in a Florida parking lot in 1990. It was linked to Tara Calico by her mother and to Michael Henley, a boy who died of exposure. Analysis by three groups was inconclusive or contradictory, and the hosts discuss why the photo's authenticity is doubtful.
topics: Polaroid photo Port St. Joe Florida

segments.title: 2008 sheriff press conference and Escobell threats
segments.summary: Sheriff Renee Rivera said in 2008 he had information and the truck may have bumped her bike, but he would make no arrests without a body. Blogger Melinda Escobell reported threats around 2010 while researching a documentary.

segments.title: Henry Brown statement and Romero conspiracy
segments.summary: A 2013 statement, given through former deputy Frank Methola, reports Henry Brown's deathbed claim that Lawrence Romero Jr. and another man admitted killing Calico. Romero Jr. died from a gunshot wound; the FBI later offered a reward in 2019.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener corrects the hosts' phone number math from an earlier episode, and the hosts sign off.
